Definition: second person singular imperative middle voice of G1492; used as imperative lo!; --behold, lo, see.
BiblicalUsage: Behold is the word that opens the door to something new. In 2 Corinthians 5:17 Paul writes that if any man be in Christ he is a new creature, behold, all things are become new, in 2 Corinthians 6:2 he cries, behold, now is the accepted time, behold, now is the day of salvation, and in Acts 1:10 two men in white apparel stand by as the disciples behold Jesus taken up.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe behold is a call to look now, not later: new in Christ, salvation today, and a risen Lord going up before their eyes.
